issues.legal_issue: The family remained joint in status until the later period established by the evidence, rather than dividing in status at the earlier time asserted.
material_facts: The parties disputed when the family divided in status; the defendants asserted an earlier division.
The witnesses relied on for the earlier period testified to a physical partition, and their testimony was disbelieved by both lower courts.
Letters between family members showed instructions and advice concerning management of family affairs through the later period.
Documents showed that family members jointly purchased properties after the asserted earlier division, and other records supported continued joint status.
issues.conclusion: The Court upheld the finding that the family did not divide in status at the earlier time asserted and divided only in the later period supported by the documentary evidence.
issues.legal_principle: The timing of a division in status is determined from the evidence as a whole. Testimony concerning a physical partition, once disbelieved, did not establish a mere division in status; contemporaneous documents showing continuing family management and joint transactions supported the finding that the family remained joint.

rule.if: partition_suit and earlier_division_claimed and oral_evidence_described_physical_partition and oral_evidence_rejected and documents_showed_later_joint_management_and_transactions

predicates.partition_suit: The proceeding sought partition of family property.
predicates.earlier_division_claimed: A party claimed that the family had divided in status at an earlier time.
predicates.oral_evidence_described_physical_partiti: The witnesses relied on for the earlier division described a physical partition rather than a division in status alone.
predicates.oral_evidence_rejected: The courts assessing the witnesses did not accept their testimony about the asserted partition.
predicates.documents_showed_later_joint_management_: Contemporaneous documents showed continuing family management or joint property transactions after the alleged earlier division.
predicates.family_status_remained_joint_until_later: The family remained joint in status until a later period supported by the evidence.

issues.definition: When a partition suit includes a rejected earlier-division claim and documents showing later joint management and transactions, the family remained joint in status until the later period.

issues.legal_issue: Property acquired in the names of family members managing a joint family may be treated as joint family property when the family had a sufficient nucleus to fund the acquisitions.
material_facts: The joint family owned extensive property, and its income was admitted to have supported acquisitions.
The family nucleus was sufficient to fund the acquisitions standing in the names of the family members.
The family members in whose names the acquisitions stood participated in managing family property.
Family account books were not produced, and the member asserting separate income did not produce his own account books.
issues.conclusion: The Court upheld the finding that acquisitions in the names of the family members who managed the family property, made before the division in status, were family acquisitions and liable to partition.
issues.legal_principle: Where a joint family possesses a nucleus sufficient to make an acquisition, a presumption arises that an acquisition standing in the name of a person managing the family property is a family acquisition. The Court relied on this principle; it cited no statutory provision or earlier case for it.

predicates.partition_suit: The proceeding sought partition of family property.
predicates.joint_family_had_sufficient_nucleus: The joint family possessed property or income sufficient to fund the disputed acquisition.
predicates.acquisition_stood_in_name_of_family_prop: The acquisition stood in the name of a person who managed family property and was made while the family remained joint in status.
predicates.acquisition_is_presumed_joint_family_pro: The acquisition is treated as joint family property unless the presumption is displaced.

issues.definition: If a partition suit concerns an acquisition made during joint status in the name of a family property manager and the family had a sufficient nucleus, the acquisition is presumed to be joint family property.
